title: Best Travel Hair Dryers UK
short: Seven compact, foldable hair dryers tested for weight, power and dual-voltage use, from a £11 budget pick to a £99 luxury model.
intro: A travel hair dryer trades some power for size, weight and a fold-flat design so it fits in a suitcase or gym bag, usually with a dual-voltage switch for use abroad. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup, where each dryer was tested on its heat and airflow settings and attachments, weighed and measured, timed from freshly washed to fully dry hair, and assessed for finish and feel both immediately after drying and after a typical day of wear. Prices are as reviewed.

products.name: 1500W Travel Dryer
products.best_for: Cheap, no-frills drying that still beats gym and hotel dryers
products.key_spec: 1.5kW, 2 heat settings, cold shot, dual voltage, foldable, 410g, no case
products.summary: The cheapest dryer on Expert Reviews' list, with a no-thrills design that's still lightweight, foldable and comfortable to use. Two speed and heat settings plus a cold shot cover the basics, and while 1,500W isn't the most powerful rating tested, it dries hair quicker than most gym, swimming pool and hotel dryers. There's no storage case, but it has a storage loop and a dual voltage switch.
pros: Lightweight, foldable and comfortable to use
cons: Not the most powerful dryer tested

products.name: 5344BU Travel Hair Dryer
products.best_for: Buyers who don't want to compromise on power while travelling
products.key_spec: 2kW, 2 heat and speed settings, concentrator nozzle, folds flat, dual voltage, 427g
products.summary: The most powerful dryer on Expert Reviews' list is also one of the cheapest: a 2,000W rating that lets you customise your blow-dry to your hair type across two heat and speed settings. It comes with a concentrator nozzle for a smooth finish and simply folds away when done, proving you don't have to sacrifice power to travel light.
pros: Great value for its power rating
cons: Only two heat and speed settings

products.name: Italia B-Travel
products.best_for: Anyone who wants a stylish, ultra-light dryer with its own case
products.key_spec: 1.4kW, 2 heat and speed settings, high-precision concentrator nozzle, dual voltage, metallic case, 370g
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this black and gold folding dryer looks the part and delivers, with a high-precision concentrator nozzle that helps smooth frizz and a dual voltage switch for worldwide use. At 370g it's one of the lightest travel dryers tested and very comfortable to use, and it comes with a fancy metallic case to keep it protected in luggage.
pros: One of the lightest travel dryers tested
Comes with a protective metallic case
cons: Less powerful than the Babyliss or Diva Intenso

products.name: Professional TourmaPro Travel Set
products.best_for: Exceptional value with a full accessory set included
products.key_spec: 1.2kW, Tourmaline Ionic Technology, 2 speed/temperature options, case, brush and comb included, dual voltage
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this exceptional value at under £20: Tourmaline Ionic Technology generates negative ions to help reduce frizz and keep hair in better condition, promising glossy salon results in a travel-friendly package. It comes with its own storage case, a brush and comb, and a concentrator nozzle, and simply folds up for storage when done.
pros: Comes with case, brush and comb

products.name: Mighty Mini
products.badge: Best for curly or afro-textured hair
products.best_for: Gentle, fast drying for hair types prone to frizz or damage
products.key_spec: 1kW, ionic technology, infra-red heat, 2 speed settings, concentrator and diffuser included, dual voltage

It comes with a concentrator nozzle and a diffuser attachment, plus a colourful matching carry bag so it's easy to spot in luggage.

Tiny size with a matching carry bag

products.name: Intenso 4000 Pro Compact Dryer
products.best_for: Fast drying with a salon-standard motor, for UK and Europe travel
products.key_spec: 2kW, 3 heat settings, ionic technology, ceramic and tourmaline grilles, 120 cubic metres/hour airflow, 450g
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this compact dryer packs a drying punch that belies its size, with a salon-standard 2kW motor and fast airflow that dries hair quickly with minimum fuss. Ceramic- and tourmaline-infused grilles leave hair looking smooth and glossy. It fits neatly into most suitcases but isn't a folding model, and there's no dual voltage option, so US travellers will need an adaptor.
pros: Ceramic and tourmaline grilles for a glossy finish
cons: No dual voltage, needs an adaptor for the US

products.name: Flight+ Travel Hair Dryer
products.best_for: Buyers who trust the ghd brand and don't mind paying extra
products.key_spec: 1.6kW, 2 temperature settings up to 65°C, removable concentrator nozzle, protective travel case, dual voltage, 453g
products.summary: Expert Reviews notes ghd's reputation for quality and style carries through to its travel dryer: a nifty device with two temperature settings capable of emitting air at 65 degrees, a removable concentrator nozzle and a protective travel case. It's not a budget tool, but comes recommended for those who trust the brand and don't mind paying a little extra.

guide.q: What's the difference between a travel dryer and a standard dryer?
guide.a: Travel dryers are primarily designed to be light and compact for easy packing, often with a folding hinge and a shorter, wider barrel for good airflow in a smaller space. They usually include a dual voltage switch so you can use them anywhere in the world, unlike most standard home dryers.

If you travel outside the UK and Europe, yes: dual voltage lets you switch between 250V and 125V so the dryer works safely on both systems. Most dryers here have it; the Diva Pro Styling Intenso 4000 doesn't, so you'd need a separate voltage adaptor for US travel.

guide.q: How much power do I need?
guide.a: The Babyliss 5344BU and Diva Intenso 4000 both offer 2kW, the most powerful of those tested, useful for drying quickly. Lower-powered options like the Amika Mighty Mini (1kW) and Bauer TourmaPro (1.2kW) trade some speed for gentler drying, which suits fine or frizz-prone hair.

guide.q: What accessories should I look for?
guide.a: Most travel dryers include a concentrator nozzle for directing airflow precisely. A carry case, like those on the Bellissima, Bauer and ghd, keeps the dryer clean and protected in luggage. If you like to diffuse curls, check compatibility, as most travel dryers don't include a diffuser (the Amika Mighty Mini is an exception).
